:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
To find the transpose, we interchange the rows and columns. 

Here, there is just a single row, so it becomes a single column:

$$
{A}^T = 
    		\left\lbrack
    		\matrix {
    5 \ 
    -1 \ 
    0 \  
    		}
    		\right\rbrack
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Transpose of a Row Vector or Column Vector

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix
    ${B} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        1 & 2 & 4 & 2\
        4 & 4 & 1 & 1\
        3 & -3 & 0 & -1
    }
    \right\rbrack.$
What are the dimensions of ${B}^T?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
When a matrix is transposed, its dimensions switch from $N \times M$ to $M \times N.$

So, since $B$ is a $3 \times 4$ matrix, the transpose ${B}^T$ is a $4\times3$ matrix.
